verdict.reason: The predecessor closes on isolated-tone localization from a fixed windowed record, all four scoped sources support the distinction between denser spectral sampling and physical resolving power, and the next brief begins only when deterministic transform evidence becomes a random-process estimator.

lesson_boundary.single_move: Estimate the frequency and coherent-gain-corrected amplitude of one isolated windowed sinusoid from a sampled main lobe, while proving that a longer FFT only densifies samples of the same finite-record DTFT and cannot resolve overlapping components.
must_include: The exact identity between an L-point zero-padded DFT and samples of the unchanged N-sample windowed DTFT.
A three-sample dB-parabola peak-location and peak-height computation, including the flat/zero-curvature boundary.
Window-dependent model bias: exactness only for an ideal Gaussian log-magnitude lobe, symmetry at bin-centered and half-bin cases, and generic bias elsewhere.
A fixed-data versus longer-observation comparison in physical frequency units.
A relative-phase two-tone counterexample in which two visible bumps have biased locations and therefore do not establish resolution.
must_not_reteach: Window definitions, endpoint smoothness, sidelobe rankings, coherent gain derivation, scalloping derivation, or ENBW derivation from windows-leakage-and-resolution.
DFT roots-of-unity derivation, FFT factorization, circular convolution, or storage ordering.
PSD, autocorrelation, periodogram bias/variance, Welch averaging, or overlap correlation; these belong to correlation-psd-and-welch.
Joint nonlinear multi-sinusoid estimation, parametric super-resolution, STFT tracking, or noise-model likelihood theory.
lesson_boundary.optional_only: A short starred aside may identify the isolated white-noise DTFT-peak estimator as an LS/ML result, but it must not become the lesson's argument or blur the next lesson's estimator boundary.

course_spine.step: Finite records trade leakage against resolution, and isolated-tone interpolation cannot manufacture observation time.
course_spine.label: Observation limits spectra

inherits: Finite observation shifts and scales the analysis-window DTFT around each sinusoid.
Main-lobe width governs close-component separation; sidelobes govern weak-neighbor masking.
Periodic window endpoints and current-record bin units are declared before metrics are compared.
C_w=sum_n w[n] calibrates a complex tone; an interior real cosine additionally uses the one-sided factor two.
Padding a fixed N-sample record changes evaluation spacing but not main-lobe width, sidelobes, coherent gain, scalloping, or ENBW.
formal_prerequisites.exact_closing_handoff: What remains unresolved is how to locate one isolated tone between displayed coordinates without mistaking a denser grid for longer observation.

inherits: An FFT is an algorithm for the declared DFT and does not change its coefficients.
A longer convenient transform length changes arithmetic and grid density, not the informative record.

continuity.required_opening_bridge: Re-anchor windows-leakage-and-resolution with a Ref and one reminder clause: the window fixed the continuous main-lobe shape and its coherent calibration; this lesson estimates the maximum between sampled coordinates without changing that shape.

forward_handoff.established_here: For one deterministic isolated sinusoid under a declared window, dense DTFT sampling plus a local peak model can estimate frequency and amplitude, with explicit model bias and resolution limits.
forward_handoff.left_open: A noise spectrum is an ensemble power quantity; one jagged magnitude-squared finite transform has persistent estimator variance even when its FFT grid is dense.
forward_handoff.required_forward_exercise: Exactly one exercise should repeat one bin's squared magnitude over at least 50 seeded equal-length white-noise records; its solution must state that padding is not averaging and Ref correlation-psd-and-welch.

inherited_claims.claim: The raw forward transform uses exp(-j omega n), with no forward normalization.
The N acquired windowed samples determine one continuous finite-record DTFT; an L-point padded DFT samples it at omega_k=2 pi k/L.
inherited_claims.origin: windows-leakage-and-resolution retrieval gate and final forward exercise

inherited_claims.claim: A denser largest-bin coordinate can reduce grid quantization error for one isolated peak while leaving physical separation unchanged.
The periodic length-N Hann has four-current-bin null-to-null width, C_w=N/2, G_c=0.5, and 1.5-bin ENBW at the nondegenerate lengths used.
inherited_claims.origin: windows-leakage-and-resolution; inherit only the main-lobe width and C_w where needed

math_conventions.support: Informative samples use 0 <= n < N; append L-N zeros only after windowing, with L >= N.
math_conventions.transform: X_L[k]=sum_{n=0}^{N-1} x[n]w[n] exp(-j 2 pi k n/L), 0 <= k < L, so X_L[k]=X_w(exp(j 2 pi k/L)).
frequency_axes: one original-record bin is f_s/N hertz; one padded-grid step is f_s/L hertz
math_conventions.window: Use the predecessor's periodic/DFT-even coefficient convention on n=0,...,N-1; do not mix symmetric N-1 denominators.

peak_interpolator.samples: Let k* be the largest sampled isolated peak and alpha, beta, gamma be 20 log10(|X_L[k*-1]|/C_w), 20 log10(|X_L[k*]|/C_w), 20 log10(|X_L[k*+1]|/C_w).
peak_interpolator.offset: p=(1/2)(alpha-gamma)/(alpha-2 beta+gamma), with the accepted local-maximum branch constrained to -1/2 <= p <= 1/2.
peak_interpolator.peak_height: b_hat=beta-(1/4)(alpha-gamma)p dB; for an analytic complex tone A_hat=10^(b_hat/20).
peak_interpolator.real_cosine_translation: For an interior positive-frequency real cosine, calibrate the raw magnitude with 2/C_w; omit the factor two at DC and even-L Nyquist, exactly as inherited from the predecessor.
peak_interpolator.boundary: If alpha-2 beta+gamma=0, no finite parabolic vertex is identified; reject the estimate rather than divide by zero. Also reject endpoints, non-local maxima, or p outside the accepted branch.

notation_changes: N is frozen as informative record/window length and L as FFT/evaluation length throughout this lesson.
The ledger formula f_k=k f_s/N applies when transform length equals N; this lesson explicitly translates it to f_k=k f_s/L.
p is a local offset in padded-grid bins, not probability, phase, or physical hertz.

misconceptions.misconception: More FFT points mean better physical resolution.
misconceptions.replacement: L controls evaluation-grid spacing; N, f_s, and w[n] control the acquired aperture and window main lobe.
misconceptions.discriminating_example: Hold the 64 Hann-windowed samples fixed and compare L=64 with L=1024, then acquire 256 informative samples at the same f_s and compare main-lobe width in hertz.

misconceptions.misconception: Two visible bumps prove that two sinusoids are resolved and their peak locations are accurate.
misconceptions.replacement: Overlapping complex window responses add with relative phase; a dip or two local maxima can occur while both component-frequency estimates remain biased.
misconceptions.discriminating_example: Use the same two equal tones and record length under in-phase and 90-degree-relative-phase cases; overlay true frequencies and fitted peak locations.

misconceptions.misconception: Three-point parabolic interpolation is an unbiased property of FFT peaks.
misconceptions.replacement: The parabola is a local model of a window-specific log-magnitude lobe; zero padding reduces the distance over which the approximation is used but does not validate an isolated-peak model under interference or low SNR.

proposed_deterministic_claims.setup: x[n]=exp(j 2 pi (10.3/64)n), 0<=n<64, periodic Hann; compare L=64 and L=1024.
proposed_deterministic_claims.claim: Grid spacing changes from 1 original bin to 1/16 original bin and largest-bin worst-case coordinate quantization changes from 1/2 to 1/32 original bin; the continuous windowed DTFT and four-original-bin null-to-null Hann width are unchanged.
proposed_deterministic_claims.status: Already deterministically established in the predecessor's forward exercise; reuse as retrieval, then deepen with parabolic interpolation.

proposed_deterministic_claims.setup: Use the brief's alpha=-12 dB, beta=0 dB, gamma=-6 dB at L-grid bins 19,20,21 with 10 Hz spacing.
proposed_deterministic_claims.claim: p=(1/2)(-12+6)/(-12-0-6)=1/6, so the fitted frequency is the bin-20 frequency plus 1.6667 Hz; the denominator boundary is zero curvature, not a frequency estimate.
proposed_deterministic_claims.status: Exact arithmetic from the frozen exercise brief.

proposed_deterministic_claims.setup: At one fixed f_s and periodic Hann, compare the same two physical tones using N=64,L=1024 and N=256,L=1024.
proposed_deterministic_claims.claim: Padding the N=64 record yields more plotted samples across the same broad lobe; acquiring N=256 narrows the Hann main lobe in hertz by a factor of four and can change a two-component separation verdict.
proposed_deterministic_claims.status: Analytic consequence of W_N and the fixed endpoint convention; future figure data must be generated from direct DTFT sums.

proposed_deterministic_claims.setup: Recreate Smith's equal-amplitude close-tone experiment with frozen frequencies, window, length, and relative phases 0 and pi/2; mark true tones and all local maxima.
proposed_deterministic_claims.claim: The pi/2 case may display two bumps before component estimates are accurate; the two-difference-frequency-cycle rectangular case is the source-supported phase-robust comparison point.
proposed_deterministic_claims.status: Source-supported deterministic experiment; freeze exact frequencies and N before figure construction and report peak-location error, not visual verdict alone.

proposed_deterministic_claims.setup: For noiseless isolated analytic tones, sweep true offset over one L-grid cell and compute three-dB-sample parabolic estimates for rectangular, periodic Hann, and four-term Blackman-Harris windows across declared L/N ratios.
proposed_deterministic_claims.claim: Increasing L/N reduces worst-case local parabolic bias for each window, while the curves differ by window and are exactly zero at bin-centered and half-bin symmetry cases; padding does not change physical main-lobe width.
proposed_deterministic_claims.status: Proposed deterministic figure contract; no numerical thresholds may enter prose until the script, convention ledger, and extrema audit are landed.

argument_order: Retrieve the unchanged-DTFT fact from the predecessor using the fixed 64-sample Hann record.
Derive the exact L-grid sampling identity and separate grid spacing from main-lobe width.
Fit the local three-point dB parabola and carry frequency plus amplitude calibration through one analytic-tone example.
Expose model bias across windows and padding factors, including the zero-curvature rejection boundary.
Break the two-bumps expectation with the relative-phase two-tone experiment and state that overlapping peaks require a different model.
Close by moving from one deterministic peak to the variance of repeated random periodograms.
keeper_quantities: L/N=16 changes the evaluation grid from 1 to 1/16 original-record bin without changing the record.
For the frozen dB triplet, p=1/6 and the 10 Hz-grid correction is +1.6667 Hz.
A fourfold increase from N=64 to N=256 narrows a same-family window main lobe in hertz by four; a padding-only change does not.
exercise_constraints: Exactly one mechanical warm-up: the frozen three-bin dB computation.
Include the zero-denominator, zero-amplitude, bin-centered, half-bin, and coincident-tone boundaries.
Include a claim-refutation using the phase-quadrature false-resolution case.
Include a strategy-choice item distinguishing isolated localization from multi-component separation.
Exactly one forward exercise reaches correlation-psd-and-welch.
